w1.title: Worked Example 1: Emitter Discharge Rate & Irrigation Duty Cycle
w1.question: A sapling bed has 10 emitters rated at 2 L/hr each, run for 3 hours. Find total water used.

steps.text: Calculate hourly bed flow: 10 emitters × 2 L/hr = 20 L/hr.
Multiply by 3 operating hours: 20 L/hr × 3 hr.
Total root-zone delivery = 60 L with minimal evaporation loss.

check.q: If 8 emitters each deliver 4 L/hr for 2 hours, how much water is supplied?

opts.m: 32 L is for 1 hour; multiply by 2 hours to get 64 L.

w2.title: Worked Example 2: Head Loss, Filter Cleaning & Pressure Uniformity
w2.question: Inlet pressure before the filter is 2.0 bar and outlet pressure drops to 1.1 bar. What should the technician do?

steps.text: Compute pressure differential: ΔP = 2.0 − 1.1 = 0.9 bar (> 0.5 bar threshold).
Shut off the solar pump valve and open the filter flush port.
Rinse the filter mesh until ΔP returns below 0.2 bar.

check.q: What does a large pressure drop between the filter inlet and outlet gauges indicate?

opts.t: The filter mesh is clogged and needs flushing

opts.m: A high ΔP across a filter is the classic sign of sediment clogging.
Inlet pressure is already 2.0 bar; the obstruction is inside the filter.

w3.title: Worked Example 3: Water-Use Efficiency vs Flood Irrigation (Jal Seva)
w3.question: Flooding a plot takes 500 L, while precision drip needs only 200 L. How much Jal Seva water is saved?

steps.text: Subtract drip usage from flood usage: 500 L − 200 L = 300 L saved.
Result: 60% water conserved per irrigation cycle.

check.q: Why does drip irrigation reduce weed growth between crop rows?

opts.t: Water is delivered only to the crop root zone, keeping inter-row soil dry

opts.m: Targeted root-zone moisture starves inter-row weeds naturally.
Water temperature is ambient; targeted placement stops weeds.
